answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by reading the shape of its interaction graph. Honest agents build dense ties across many clusters, while a Sybil farm forms a tight clique attached to the network by only a few bridge edges, like a whisper through a single narrow door. The network throttles such weakly attached identities until they earn diverse, sustained relationships. A beacon of trust is thus a broad pattern of connection, not one credential, and forging it costs an attacker months of genuine interaction, not just new keys, much as an opal is trusted only after many hands examine it.
